title: People & Operations Intern
description:

We're looking for a People & Operations Intern to help build how Simular works as a company; not just behind a desk, but out in the world. You'll support hiring, onboarding, IT compliance, office management, and employee experience, while also representing Simular at hackathons, career fairs, and community events.

This is a great role if you want to see how an early-stage AI company actually runs, from the inside out. This role requires a full-time commitment.



What you'll do

Hiring & Talent Engineering

• Support the full hiring pipeline: post roles, screen resumes, coordinate interviews, follow up with candidates

• Help with onboarding new hires: equipment, accounts, welcome materials, first-week logistics

• Represent Simular at career fairs, university events, and recruiting meetups



Events & Community

• Help organize and attend hackathons, tech meetups, and industry events

• Coordinate team events, offsites, and internal culture moments

• Be a face of Simular at external events: you'll meet candidates, partners, and community members in person



Operations & Compliance

• Help find and manage office spaces

• Assist with IT compliance: device management, security policies, access controls

• Coordinate with external vendors: insurance, IT providers, and other service partners

• Support employment compliance across multiple jurisdictions: contracts, visa applications, labor law requirements

• Maintain employee records and keep things organized



AI & Process Automation

• Identify repetitive ops workflows and help automate them using AI tools, no-code platforms, or scripts

• Build and maintain internal automations: onboarding checklists, compliance reminders, candidate pipeline tracking

• Develop your AI literacy by working daily with AI agents and LLMs as part of how we operate

• Help the team stay on the frontier: test new AI tools, share what works, and document best practices





You might be a fit if

• You're organized, detail-oriented, and can juggle multiple tasks without dropping balls

• You communicate clearly and professionally

• You're proactive; you see something that needs doing and you do it

• You're curious about AI and eager to build real AI literacy, not just use LLMs, but understand how AI tools can transform workflows

• You're comfortable with ambiguity and figuring things out on your own

• You're a people person who's energized by events and face-to-face interactions

• You care about building a great workplace, not just running one



Bonus

• Prior internship in HR, people ops, or startup environments

• Experience organizing events, clubs, or student organizations

description:

You'll work directly with the founders and GTM lead on the analysis behind our go-to-market decisions, and you'll see your recommendations turn into action quickly.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Research the agent and AI tooling landscape: map competitors, positioning, and pricing, and turn it into clear briefs the team can act on

 - Size and segment target markets, then build a point of view on which segments we should pursue first

 - Talk to users and prospects, synthesize what you hear, and translate patterns into product and GTM recommendations

 - Support early sales motions: prospect research, account briefs, and follow-up materials for founder-led conversations

 - Build lightweight models and analyses that answer real questions, such as pipeline health, funnel conversion, and channel efficiency

 - Write crisp memos and decks that help the team make a call, not just admire the data

title: Product & User Operations Intern
description:

Our users are doing things with autonomous agents that nobody has done before, which means they hit problems nobody has documented. Sitting between those users and the product team is one of the highest-signal seats in the company.

You'll be the person who knows what users are actually struggling with, and who makes sure that knowledge reaches the people who can fix it.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Handle frontline user support: answer support email, Discord questions, and tickets clearly and quickly

 - Own the feedback loop from users into the product backlog: triage, categorize, and quantify what people are hitting

 - Support release operations: track what is shipping, write release notes, and verify things work as intended after they land

 - Maintain help docs, canned responses, and the knowledge base so common questions stop being asked twice

 - Track feature timelines, release notes, and delivery progress, and keep the team honest about dates

 - Monitor product metrics such as activation, retention, and feature adoption, and report what's changing

 - Run onboarding and activation analysis: find where new users stall, and propose product fixes rather than workarounds

 - Help operationalize agent quality: review real agent runs, catalogue failure modes, and feed them back to product and research

 - Advocate for the user in product discussions, with evidence rather than anecdote


YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF

 - You're pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in any field, or equivalent experience

 - You write clearly and kindly, especially when replying to someone who is frustrated

 - You're organized and reliable, and you follow through without being chased

 - You're comfortable with data: you can pull numbers, spot a trend, and explain it

 - You're curious about how products get built and want to be close to that process

 - You can hold context across many small threads without dropping things

Bonus: prior support, community, or product ops experience, or you've run a Discord community

title: Design Engineer Intern
description:

Designing for autonomous agents is genuinely unsolved. When software acts on its own, the usual patterns stop working: how does someone watch an agent, trust it, correct it, or take back control? There's no established playbook, which makes this an unusually interesting place to design.

You'll work on real product surfaces that ship to users, with the support of an experienced team.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design end-to-end product surfaces for agent experiences, from concept through shipped interface

 - Explore new interaction models for how people observe, guide, and interrupt autonomous agents

 - Build working prototypes in code, not just clickable mockups, so ideas get tested against reality early

 - Use AI tools aggressively to compress the distance between an idea and something running

 - Run lightweight user testing and turn what you learn into design decisions

 - Contribute to and help maintain our design system for consistency across the product

 - Work closely with engineers so your designs survive contact with implementation

 - Care about craft: spacing, motion, states, and the details most people never consciously notice


YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF

 - You're pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Design, HCI, or a related field, or equivalent experience

 - You have a portfolio showing original thinking, not just competent execution of familiar patterns

 - You're fluent in Figma and comfortable prototyping interaction and motion

 - You can build what you design: comfortable with HTML/CSS/JS or React, or you vibe-code your way to a working prototype

 - You're AI-fluent: you use AI tools daily in your design and building workflow, and you have a point of view on where they help and where they don't

 - You can explain why you made a decision, not just present the outcome

title: Generative AI Researcher Intern
description:
MESHY RESEARCH INTERNSHIP PROGRAM

We’re looking for exceptional research interns who are passionate about AI, graphics, and building world-class products together with us.


What we’re looking for:

 - Able to commit to a full-time internship for 12 weeks or longer

 - Intend to join Meshy full-time after graduation (ideally graduating from 9/2026-9/2027, but later is also acceptable)

 - Open to undergraduate, master's, or PhD students

 - Strong in technical fundamentals, with a spirit of innovation and willingness to challenge yourself
   

Who You Are

 - You are a talented, hands-on researcher who thrives in a fast-paced environment, is self-directed, a team player, and knows how to get things done efficiently. 

 - You have deep understanding of the transformer architecture, have strong python and tensor programming skills, have a vision for AI beyond linear sequences, and you believe in "the scaling law". 

 - You can translate high-level goals into concrete research and implementation steps, set an approach, and follow through. When it's time to explain your ideas, you bring clarity to complex technical issues. 

 - You are not afraid of confronting new ideas, and you are eager to share your knowledge with the team. You use these skills to create real-world benefits for our researchers, engineers, and millions of users, and you are excited to help advance our effort to push the state of the art of AI that understands and generates 3D worlds.
   

Who We Are

At Meshy, we believe 3D creation should be boundless and accessible. Our mission statement is simple: unleash creativity. We built a full pipeline for 3D content ranging from text / image to 3D, texturing, texture editing, animation rigging, etc. We also built a vibrant community for our creators, where people can share their work, take inspiration from others, and even use it as an asset marketplace for their games and prototypes. We are the market leader in 3D generative AI, recognized as the No.1 in popularity among 3D AI tools (according to 2024 A16Z Games survey), and we generate real value and is used by enterprises (including Meta, Square Enix, Deepmind, etc.) and millions of end users. Meshy is used in game and film production, in 3D printing, in industrial product design, in enablement of novel product features such as user-generated content, and even in training and simulation for robotics and physical AI.




Your Next Challenge

As a core member of the team of research scientists and machine learning engineers at Meshy, you will work towards Meshy's long-term ambitious research goals while identifying intermediate milestones.




If you are interested in our research on Artist-level Low-poly mesh generation models, you will join us to:

 - Design, train and finetune 3D generative models from covering pre-training, post-training, and emerging paradigms in autoregressive and discrete diffusion.

 - Analyze, discretize and process meshes and design tokenizers for generative models to ingest.

 - Accelerate model training from an architectural view. Maximize memory usage and elliminate pipeline bubbles in both CPU and GPU.

 

If your obsession lies in creating superior visual appearances, join our Texture & Material Research efforts to:

 - Redefine 3D texture generation. Advance the state-of-the-art in Diffusion and Auto-regressive models to produce crisp, high-resolution textures with robust geometric consistency.

 - Deliver "Game-Ready" assets. Focus on generating full PBR stacks that react realistically to lighting, bridging the gap between generative AI and professional production pipelines.
   


📍 LOCATION

We are based in Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen - you’re welcome to join us in any of these offices.

title: Applied Researcher Intern
description:
WHO YOU ARE

You are a motivated student or recent graduate who is passionate about building systems — someone who gets excited about automating workflows, writing clean and reliable code, and making complex pipelines actually work. You have a solid foundation in computer graphics and engineering, and you're eager to apply that in the context of cutting-edge generative AI.

You might come from a software engineering background with a deep interest in 3D and computer graphics, or from a Technical Art background with strong programming skills. Either way, you thrive when engineering and creativity intersect.

You care about real-world creator impact: you're enthusiastic about how generative AI can comprehend, understand, and elevate human creativity — and you want to be part of building that future.


YOUR NEXT CHALLENGE

As an intern on the Applied Research team at Meshy, you will help build the connective tissue between our generative models, 3D data, and the tools that researchers and artists use every day. Your focus will be on making workflows reliable, automated, and scalable.

The essential functions include, but are not limited to:

 - Build and automate internal pipelines that connect our generative AI models, 3D data, and production tools — turning fragile manual scripts into reliable, repeatable systems.

 - Develop evaluation infrastructure that allows researchers to consistently assess model quality and get visual feedback in hours rather than days.

 - Integrate with DCC tools such as Maya, Blender, or Houdini to support automated asset processing, transformation, and quality validation.

 - Write clean, well-documented, and reproducible code that the broader team can rely on and build upon.

 - Identify and eliminate technical bottlenecks across the pipeline, keeping workflows scalable as the team and model complexity grow.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Digital Media, Animation, Game Development, or a related field.

 - Strong programming skills in Python — this is a must. You are comfortable writing clean, maintainable, production-quality code, not just scripts.

 - Solid foundation in computer graphics — you understand how 3D content is structured, rendered, and processed at a technical level (e.g., mesh geometry, shaders, rendering pipelines).

 - Genuine interest in generative AI — you've explored image, video, or 3D generation tools and are curious about how they work under the hood.

 - Good communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively across research and engineering contexts.

Nice to have:

 - Proficiency in C++ is a strong plus.

 - Hands-on experience with DCC tools such as Maya, Blender, or Houdini.

 - Familiarity with concepts like mesh topology, UV mapping, materials, or rigging.

 - A portfolio or examples of past 3D or technical work (personal projects are welcome).


A LITTLE MORE ABOUT MESHY.AI http://meshy.ai

Trusted by Meta, Square Enix, DeepMind, and more, Meshy is redefining 3D creation with generative AI. We empower artists, designers, engineers, hobbyists, and makers to bring immersive worlds, characters, and experiences to reality in minutes instead of months.

We value intelligence and the pursuit of knowledge. We are a global team of generative-AI pioneers, computer-graphics veterans, and product builders who believe human expression and enjoyment is the ultimate frontier of computing.

We care deeply about our work, our users, and each other. Empathy and passion drive us forward. We have a culture of directness and truthfulness — being direct is the most sincere form of trust and care.

We trust our instincts and are not afraid to take bold risks. Meshy was born from a few-hour prototype. Innovation requires courage.


LOCATION & WORK ENVIRONMENT

This role is based on-site in our Shanghai office. We believe great collaboration happens in person, and you'll have the opportunity to work closely with our Applied Research team day-to-day.

We are a fast-paced startup and we work hard. You should be able to:

 - Clearly communicate ideas and findings to teammates from different backgrounds.

 - Pay close attention to detail while keeping the bigger picture in mind.

 - Work through ambiguous problems and meet tight deadlines.

title: Early Adopter & Product Builder Intern, Creative AI
description:
🎨 ABOUT OPENART

OpenArt is an AI Storytelling and Visual Creation Platform used by millions worldwide. We’re building the next generation of creative tools powered by cutting-edge AI, enabling anyone to create videos, visuals, characters, and stories with unprecedented speed and imagination. We believe the future of creativity is AI-native, and we’re shaping that future.

🚀 Why Join OpenArt

 - Real impact through leadership exposure — work directly with C-level leaders and the key decision-making committee, with opportunities for your ideas and judgment to shape a product used by more than 10M users worldwide.

 - A direct role in growth strategy — help leadership assess where to expand, which customers and partners to prioritize, and how to plan for scale.

 - Exposure to the creative AI ecosystem — research the market and gather insights from creative professionals, agencies, model providers, operators and investors.

 - Return offer opportunities — strong interns will be considered for full-time roles across product, engineering, research and GTM.


ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll help shape how OpenArt feels to use. This role is for builders with a technical background and strong product taste: people who follow AI progress closely and know how to turn new capabilities into features creative professionals love.




EMPLOYMENT TYPE

Year-round internship with rolling start dates: full-time in summer, part-time (15–20 hrs/week) during the fall and spring semesters. Minimum 3-month commitment




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Track tech progress: follow new AI models, tools and tech trends at the cutting edge, often before public launch through early access, understand what each makes possible, and bring a regular take on what OpenArt should adopt or build.

 - Turn ideas into features: translate new capabilities into feature ideas, prototype them, and work with designers and engineers to ship them.

 - Test hands-on: run usability tests on new features and benchmark competing creative AI products, then form a clear judgment on what's great, what's broken and what to do next, and get the team aligned on it.

 - Partner across teams: work with Growth and Community on creator programs, challenges and showcases that highlight great work made on OpenArt.

 - Stay close to users: listening to users is part of doing this job well. Talk with them every day (interviews, Discord, social), understand what they need, and let that shape every feature you push for.

TURN CUSTOMER TICKETS INTO AUTOMATED TESTS

Success here is measured by the share of customer-reported regressions your tests would have caught, and by how much faster CX can confirm a reported issue is real.




MAP USER WORKFLOWS INTO TESTABLE MOMENTS

Before a test exists, someone has to break a workflow like "upload a video, get clips, export to TikTok" into its discrete steps, decision points and failure modes, and rank them by how many customers they touch. Customer empathy: Must-have. You want to understand what the user was trying to do, not just what broke. You read a ticket and see a person with a deadline, not a bug ID.

title: Data Science Intern
description:
ABOUT MERCOR



Mercor’s mission is to organize human intelligence for the AI economy. We build the infrastructure that enables frontier AI labs and enterprises to train, evaluate, and improve AI on real-world professional work. More than five million experts have joined our network, and we pay out over $5 million daily for their knowledge and expertise.

We built our training and evaluation infrastructure alongside the world’s leading AI labs. Now, we’re bringing those capabilities to enterprises across industries, enabling them to train, evaluate, and improve AI using their own expertise and standards. Our APEX benchmarks measure how AI performs on economically valuable work, while our enterprise evaluations and post-training capabilities turn those insights into measurable improvements across real-world workflows.

Our work sits at the intersection of frontier AI, human expertise, and real-world application. We’re solving problems few companies have encountered, with the opportunity to influence what the world’s most advanced AI systems become capable of doing. We’re looking for people who bring different perspectives, take ownership, exercise sound judgment, and hold themselves to an exceptionally high standard. You’ll have the opportunity to do consequential work alongside talented colleagues who challenge one another, collaborate openly, and share a commitment to excellence.

Mercor is profitable and recently raised a $750 million Series D at a $20 billion valuation. We work in person five days a week in San Francisco, New York, and London.



About the Role

As a Data Science Intern at Mercor, you’ll join a fast-moving, metrics-driven engineering team whose work shapes decisions across the company. You’ll analyze data that directly affects ranking, hiring efficiency, candidate experience and revenue, work with production datasets from your first week, and ship insights that product and engineering act on.

You’ll start on the analyses and tooling your team has wanted but hasn’t had the hands for, and as needs come up you’ll take deep ownership of them, with a named mentor alongside you. You’ll move quickly while keeping a high bar for analytical rigor, clarity and statistical correctness.



Where You’ll Work

Interns start on a rolling basis, so summer, spring and fall terms all work. About three weeks before your start we’ll match you to one of two teams:

 - Product Data Science. The data science function for the marketplace and talent platform: metrics for matching, ranking and hiring efficiency, event instrumentation and data integrity, experiments on the candidate and customer experience, and scoring models that change who gets surfaced for which role.

 - Applied AI Data Science. The data science function inside the org that delivers human data and evaluations to frontier AI labs: operational analytics for live customer projects, automated quality control that gates what ships, and evaluation science that shows a lab where its model breaks and why.
   
   

What You’ll Work On

 - Defining north-star metrics and feature-level KPIs for ranking, interview analytics and payouts

 - Designing A/B tests and quasi-experiments and turning results into product decisions within days

 - Building dashboards and lightweight data models so teams can self-serve insights

 - Instrumenting events with engineers and improving data quality, observability and latency

 - Prototyping models, from baselines to gradient boosting, to improve matching and scoring

 - Evaluating LLM-powered systems through rubric design, human-in-the-loop experiments and guardrail testing
   
   

What We’re Looking For

 - Pursuing a degree in a quantitative field, graduating 2027 (potentially 2028)

 - Strong fundamentals in statistics, SQL and Python

 - Experience with experiment design, causal reasoning and data analysis

 - Clear communication with engineers, product managers and leadership

 - Curiosity about LLM evaluation, retrieval, ranking or marketplace dynamics

 - Excited to work in person in San Francisco

 - Nice to have: dbt, dashboarding tools, recommendation or search metrics, LLM and agent evaluation
   
   

Why Mercor

 - Impact: your work powers how frontier AI labs train and deploy their models

 - Learning: early exposure to frontier AI research and engineering

 - Growth: a high-velocity team where interns ship to production
   
   

Compensation and Benefits

 - $10K housing bonus if you live within 0.5 miles of our office during your internship

 - $1.5K monthly stipend for meals/rideshare

 - Health, dental and vision insurance

 - 401(k) eligibility

title: Mechatronics Intern
description:
Fundamentally, a builder. Someone who loves to make robots real. We want someone who’s as comfortable debugging a CAN bus issue as they are machining a bracket — an individual who thinks in systems, and who gets excited by tight integration between mechanical, electrical, and embedded design. You’ll join the core Hardware Engineering team at Physical Intelligence who is supporting the robots that power PI’s data collection and model training operations.

The Team

The core Hardware Engineering team designs and builds the robotic arms, mobile platforms, and end-effectors that underpin PI’s data collection and model training operations. They work across mechanical, electrical, embedded, and software disciplines to iterate quickly on prototypes, bring up new subsystems, and keep the fleet performant in real-world environments.

In This Role You Will

 - Subsystem Design & Test: Design, build, and test key subsystems for various robotic arms and mobile platforms — including actuation, sensing, enclosures, and power systems.

 - Hands-On Prototyping: Work hands-on with prototypes in our hardware lab, including bring-up, assembly, calibration, and reliability testing of arms, lifts, mobile bases, and end-effectors.

 - Cross-Disciplinary Integration: Integrate cross-disciplinary inputs from mechanical, electrical, and software teams to root-cause mission-critical issues and drive high-level system performance.

 - Data-Driven Iteration: Analyze data from deployments to inform design iteration and reliability improvements.

 - Full-Stack Subsystem Ownership: Own the full stack of a subsystem from CAD to PCB to bench testing.

What We Hope You’ll Bring

 - Completed 3A Mechanical or Mechatronics Engineering. Students below 3A with exceptional projects, GitHubs, portfolios, and work experience will also be considered.

 - Strong mechanical and electromechanical design fundamentals (dynamic loading, FEA, DFM).

 - Familiarity with embedded and mechatronic systems (CAN, BLDC control, motor controllers).

 - Proficiency in CAD (NX, OnShape, SolidWorks) and rapid prototyping tools (3D printing — SLA and FDM — laser cutting).

 - Basic electrical design and debug (schematics, soldering, test equipment).

 - Data-driven debugging and test planning (Python, MATLAB, or similar).

Bonus Points

 - Prior experience in robotics, autonomous systems, or hardware startups.

title: Base Labs Fellowship
description:
ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F https://www.baseten.co/blog/announcing-our-series-f/, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.



ABOUT BASE LABS

Base Labs is a research lab pushing the frontier of open-source LLMs. We think intelligence should be democratized, not controlled by a handful of closed labs and we think very few teams are actually positioned to do something about that.

Backed by Baseten's training and inference infrastructure, we have the compute, resources, and talent to take on hard problems at the frontier and open-source what we learn along the way.

Our mission is to help build a world where intelligence isn't concentrated, but spread across an ecosystem of models that anyone can build on. That mission shapes what we choose to work on, how we work on it, and who we want in the room.

We are accepting applications on a rolling basis for our first cohort of Base Labs Fellows.



BASE LABS FELLOWSHIP OVERVIEW

The Base Labs Fellowship is designed to give researchers exposure to what frontier research looks like in industry. We provide funding, mentorship, and full support to our fellows, with the goal of producing rigorous, published research that shapes both the open-source ecosystem and Baseten's technical roadmap.

We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis. 



WHAT TO EXPECT

 - 3 months of full-time research from our San Francisco office

 - A dedicated 1:1 mentorship from a senior researcher

 - $18,750 Stipend (per month) / $225,000 annually

 - Funding for compute and other research expenses

 - Opportunities to publish and present at top venues, including ICML, NeurIPS, and ICLR

 - A clear path to a full-time offer for the strongest performers


YOUR MENTORS

Each fellow is matched 1:1 with one of three senior researchers.

Potential mentors include:

 - Michael Psenka

 - Max Kirkby

 - Charles O’Neill

Note: You're welcome to research mentors' prior work, but all applications must go through the official process below, not the mentors directly.




WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

A quick note on our view on talent.

Many of the labs that exist today run a credentialist talent model. Concentrate the most already-legible researchers, and assume the concentration compounds. The best researchers in this field are very often not yet legible. Research engineers who have spent years inside a production stack and developed insights no PhD program teaches; PhDs working on the wrong-shaped problem at the right-shaped lab; operators who have been close to real systems long enough to see things traditional researchers have never had to see. If you don’t have the usual qualifications and are doing exceptional work, we’d love to chat.

For the sake of providing some directional criteria for potential fits for this fellowship:

 - Are enrolled in or have recently completed a PhD in ML, AI, statistics, or a closely related field

 - Have a publication record or research portfolio that demonstrates original, rigorous thinking

 - Care about what your work is in service of - not just the problem, but why it matters

 - Want to operate with autonomy and don't need a defined roadmap to do your best work

 - Are excited to be in San Francisco for the duration of the program, fully embedded in the team

 - Are drawn to the idea of building a research culture, not just participating in one
   
   

WHY BASE LABS?

 - 1:1 by design. Three fellows, three mentors. You will not get lost.

 - Real stakes. Your research feeds directly into decisions about what Baseten builds and what workloads it pursues. The line from your work to the product is short.

 - A founding moment. We are building Base Labs from scratch. The first cohort shapes what it becomes the culture, the research agenda, the brand.

 - Full support. Housing, meals, travel, and compute are all handled. We remove every barrier between you and the work.

 - A clear path forward. Top performers are considered for a full-time role.

NOTE: The benefits listed below are only applicable to full-time hires. 



BENEFITS

 - Competitive compensation, including meaningful equity

 - (U.S. only) 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance for employee and dependents

 - Paid parental leave

 - Fertility and family-building stipend through Carrot

 - Exposure to a variety of ML startups, offering unparalleled learning and networking opportunities.
